speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh
text: asked the Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) how programmes such as the Sport Excellence Potential (spexPotential) account for sports where athletes peak later, including how long athletes can be supported before reaching senior representation; and (b) how the Ministry ensures such athletes are not disadvantaged by early progression benchmarks.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Our Sport Excellence (spex) framework provides comprehensive support for athletes across different stages of their sporting journey.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: It seeks to retain athletes early in the developmental pathway and also, long enough for them to realise their aspirations and achieve their full potential.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: It bridges our athletes’ journey towards the spexScholarship programme and sporting success at the Asian and world levels.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The framework of spex programmes – spexScholarship, spexPotential and spexCarding – also allows us to calibrate the level of support during various stages of an athlete’s sporting career.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This means athletes will be supported throughout their sporting journey, even if their performance fluctuates from time to time.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: For example, we would be familiar with Theresa Goh, our Paralympian swimmer.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: She is also a late bloomer for para shooting.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: She took up the sport recently and won a gold and a silver at the recent ASEAN Para Games.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Now as a shooter, she is supported by spexCarding at 38 years old.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Once again, our aim is really to help every athlete achieve their fullest sporting potential.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: To do so, we work very closely with our partners, especially the National Sports Associations (NSAs) to develop our athletes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Together, we establish multiple pathways to account for differences in athletes’ development pathways and the characteristics of each sport, so that we can really support all our athletes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: It is reassuring to know that within our sporting framework, that we are an inclusive system, not just in terms of athletes who are differently abled, but also across different ages as well.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: I bring up this question, because at the recent SEA Games it was reported that one of the sprinters who won a gold medal was not on the spex programme, despite him having been a former SEA Games medalist, having also competed in the Asian Games and in the Commonwealth Games.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: And so, my understanding was that these performances, while exemplary and something that we celebrate, fell outside of the window for consideration in awarding the spexScholarships and the spex grants.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: So, my question to the Acting Minister is whether the Ministry would consider extending the window for consideration of these spex grants, especially in relation to older athletes?

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: And one reason for that is because as older athletes have different and more varied life circumstances.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: If you are talking about younger athletes, I think their life circumstances are more homogeneous – they go to school and they participate in sport.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: With older athletes, they work, they take care of family, they have a variety of responsibilities and that takes them off the high performance track.
